headline: MV June Aster Death Toll Rises to 77 After Rescued Survivor Dies
seoTitle: MV June Aster Death Toll Rises to 77 | FMB News
seoDescription: Local authorities in Coron say the MV June Aster death toll has risen to 77 after a rescued survivor died, while 12 people remain missing.
deck: Coron health and disaster officials say one rescued survivor died in hospital, raising the confirmed toll to 77 as 12 people remain missing.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: Ferry Fire Off Coron Leaves at Least 5 Dead as Search Continues
continuesFrom.whatChanged: Since FMB News first reported the ferry fire, recovery operations raised the toll to 76. Coron health and disaster officials now say a rescued survivor died in hospital, bringing the confirmed death toll to 77 while 12 people remain missing.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The confirmed death toll from the MV June Aster ferry fire off Coron, Palawan has risen to 77 after one of the rescued survivors died at the Culion Sanitarium and General Hospital, according to the Coron Municipal Health Office and Coron Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office as reported by GMA News on Wednesday, September 16.

The latest local-authority accounting reported by GMA News lists 77 deaths, 43 people rescued and 12 people still missing. The figures remain subject to reconciliation as recovery and identification work continues.

sections.heading: What changed since FMB's earlier reports
paragraphs: FMB News first reported the disaster on September 10 when authorities had confirmed at least five deaths. A September 12 continuation recorded a death toll of 76 after rescuers recovered additional remains from the burned vessel.

The latest increase is not another recovery from the wreck: local authorities say a person who had been rescued later died in hospital. That change in the casualty accounting is independently newsworthy and is being published as a continuation rather than overwriting the earlier record.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The MV June Aster caught fire on September 9 while sailing near Coron after departing Manila. Authorities previously reconciled the number of people aboard to 132 after two people listed on the original 134-person manifest reported that they had not boarded.

The Philippine Coast Guard has said Captain Roel Sarmiento voluntarily appeared at the vessel operator's Palawan office and is expected to be questioned by investigators about the incident and his whereabouts after the fire.

Authorities have not issued a final finding on the cause of the fire. Survivor accounts and preliminary descriptions of events aboard the vessel are not being presented by FMB News as a determination of cause.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The death of a person who had initially survived the disaster changes the confirmed human toll while families of the 12 people still missing continue to await answers.

The investigation also remains important for Philippine maritime safety because it may establish whether equipment, cargo conditions, emergency procedures, crew actions, regulatory compliance or another factor contributed to the disaster.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: Twelve people remain missing in the latest reported accounting. Identification of recovered victims and reconciliation of the final casualty list are continuing.
The cause and point of origin of the fire have not been conclusively established, and no final finding of responsibility has been issued by the investigating authorities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for further casualty reconciliation from Coron authorities and the Philippine Coast Guard, identification of victims, recovery of those still missing, and formal findings from the Coast Guard and Maritime Industry Authority investigations.

sections.heading: Reader note
paragraphs: This is a developing story. FMB News will continue the record when a material new fact is verified.

audit.socialCaption: DEVELOPING: Coron health and disaster officials say the MV June Aster death toll has risen to 77 after a rescued survivor died in hospital. Twelve people remain missing, while the cause of the September 9 ferry fire remains under investigation.
verificationNotes: GMA News reported the new 77-death accounting at 9:27 a.m. on September 16, attributing it to the Coron Municipal Health Office and Coron MDRRMO.

The specific new fact is the death of a previously rescued survivor at Culion Sanitarium and General Hospital; FMB News clearly attributes that update rather than presenting an unsupported independent count.
Philstar independently confirms the immediately preceding accounting of 76 dead and 12 missing and the Coast Guard's continuing investigation, providing continuity and corroborating context.
The cause of the fire remains unresolved and is not stated as fact.
The continuation links to FMB News' earliest September 10 report, preserving the historical chain.

The hero is a genuinely relevant Philippine Coast Guard file photograph hosted on Wikimedia Commons and marked public domain in the Philippines under PD-PhilippinesGov. It is explicitly captioned as a file image and not as a photograph of the hospital death.
